subject: Storix AI — Load test handoff & SLO alignment
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@storix.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Storix AI — Load test handoff & SLO alignment

Hi Elena — thanks for the time today. Quick recap of what we agreed and the proposed handoff plan so your engineers can run the customer-led test next week.

Recap / SLO targets we captured on the call:
- P95 latency target (text generation, 512 tokens): < 200 ms
- Median latency: < 80 ms
- Sustained throughput goal: 500 req/s across the service (peak windows up to 700 req/s for 10m bursts)
- Concurrent streaming sessions: up to 120 simultaneous streaming connections (50–120 range; please confirm expected connection churn)
- Failure budget: < 1% 5xx across the load window

Logistics / next steps (proposed):
1) Attach k6 script (short smoke + steady-state profile) and a Redwood runbook for allowlist + test accounts — see attachments.
2) Please confirm the planned test window (we tentatively proposed Tue 2027-04-27 08:00-11:00 PT).
3) Provide the IP ranges you can call from / or let us know if you want Redwood to provide a proxy endpoint to avoid allowlist work.
4) We’ll provision a test model slot and a set of test API keys (limited quota) for the run — we’ll send these once the allowlist is in place.
5) Monica (ops) will be on-call during the window for immediate support; Grace (SRE) will watch the logs and latency dashboards.

Attachments included: storix_k6_script_v1.js (k6 script), redwood-allowlist-template.txt, storix-loadtest-runbook.pdf

Please confirm the window and the person who will own the run on your side (Samir for infra?). Once you confirm we’ll finalize the IP list and handoff checklist.

Cheers,
Marcus
Enterprise AE — Redwood Inference
marcus@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

---
(Attachment stubs: storix_k6_script_v1.js [javascript k6 script], redwood-allowlist-template.txt [text], storix-loadtest-runbook.pdf [pdf])

From: Elena Park <elena@storix.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samir Gupta <samir@storix.ai>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Storix AI — Load test handoff & SLO alignment

Thanks Marcus — this is helpful. Samir will own the run from our side. Quick answers and a couple requests: 

Confirmations:
- Test window: Tue 2027-04-27 08:00-11:00 PT works for us.
- Samir will be primary; I’ll be available as backup.
- Our expected steady-state throughput target is 450–500 req/s; we might push a single 15-minute spike to 750 req/s mid-window.

Requests / clarifications:
- Can you confirm the exact IP list Redwood needs to allow (CIDR blocks)? We run through a corporate firewall and need CIDRs to open.
- For streaming sessions: our client retains an open websocket per user; typical churn is ~30%/10m. We want to validate sustained memory and KV-cache behavior under that churn.
- We’d like the k6 script to include a short ramp (10m), a 40m steady-state, then a 10m spike. Can you add that pattern to the attached script and re-send?

We downloaded the attachments — thanks. Samir, looping you in to coordinate infra.

—Elena
Director, Platform Engineering
Storix AI
elena@storix.ai

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@storix.ai>
Cc: Samir Gupta <samir@storix.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Storix AI — Load test handoff & SLO alignment

Elena / Samir — great, thanks for the fast reply. I updated the plan inline and attached a variant of the k6 script with the ramp / steady / spike pattern you described (storix_k6_script_v1.js -> storix_k6_script_v1.js). A couple operational notes below: 

IP allowlist:
- Preferred: If you can allowlist our agent IPs, please add the following CIDRs to your firewall: 34.210.16.0/20, 52.202.96.0/19, 18.205.32.0/20. (These are our regional load-generation egress blocks; confirm with your security team.)
- Alternative: If that’s difficult, we can provision a temporary proxy endpoint (single IP) and route traffic through it; let us know and we’ll send a separate IP.

Test accounts / keys:
- We’ll create a test API key scoped to the top-level model and limit quota to 100k tokens for the window. Expect an email from support@redwoodinference.com with the key once allowlist is confirmed.

Observability and SLOs:
- Grace will open a shared dashboard (token-latency, p95, p99, error rates, tail latencies per model). We’ll share a Grafana link 1h before the window.
- If p95 exceeds 200 ms for more than 5m continuously we’ll mark the window as "needs follow-up" and collect flamegraphs and kernel traces for analysis.

On-call / escalation:
- Monica will be on-call during the run and reachable at monica@redwoodinference.com / +1 (415) 555-0283. Please Slack or call for immediate help.

Samir — can you confirm you can open the three CIDR blocks or whether you want the proxy option? Also confirm if your team prefers k6 or Locust — we included a k6 script by default because it’s lighter for HTTP patterns; if you prefer Locust we’ll convert.

Thanks — I’ll stand by for the allowlist confirmation and will lock the dashboard URL once Grace creates it.

Best,
Marcus
Enterprise AE — Redwood Inference

- We’ll take the k6 script as-is for the first run. If we see protocol-level issues we’ll switch to a Locust variant for finer websocket control.
- For streaming sessions, we’ll run a smaller rehearsal on Mon 2027-04-26 16:00-16:30 PT (short ramp + 10m steady) to validate connection handling before the Tue full window. Can your team be available for that rehearsal?
